ACID: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability, the guarantees of a database transaction
ACK: acknowledgement, a TCP flag confirming received data
AMQP: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol, the protocol RabbitMQ speaks
AOP: aspect-oriented programming, adding behaviour such as transactions around methods without editing them
ARM: Arm (a family of processor designs, originally Acorn RISC Machine)
ASCII: American standard code for information interchange
ASR: automatic speech recognition, turning speech into text
AVL: Adelson-Velsky and Landis, the inventors of the self-balancing tree
AWQ: activation-aware weight quantisation, a GPU-oriented way of compressing model weights
BIND: Berkeley Internet Name Domain (a DNS server)
BLEU: bilingual evaluation understudy, a score for how many word sequences a text shares with a reference text
BM25: Best Matching 25, the standard keyword-ranking formula: rare words count more, repeats count less, long documents don't win by length
BMP: bitmap, the uncompressed Windows image file format
BSD: Berkeley Software Distribution, a family of Unix systems
BSP: binary space partitioning, splitting space with planes into a tree
BYOK: bring your own key, users supplying their own API key
C10K: the problem of handling ten thousand concurrent connections on one machine
C2PA: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, whose content credentials record how media was made
CD: continuous delivery or continuous deployment, releasing every change that passes the pipeline
CDC: change data capture, reading a database's change log to stream every committed change
CIJ: continuous ink jet, a printing technique that breaks a stream of ink into droplets
COMSOL: COMSOL Multiphysics, a commercial finite-element simulation package
CoT: chain of thought, asking a model to reason step by step before answering
CPLEX: IBM's commercial linear and integer programming solver
CPM: critical path method, for finding a project's duration and its zero-slack activities; also CPM.cmake, a CMake package manager
CQRS: command query responsibility segregation, separate models for writing and reading
CRIME: Compression Ratio Info-leak Made Easy (an attack)
CRT: cathode ray tube, the electron-beam display used in older monitors and TVs
CSI: Container Storage Interface, how Kubernetes mounts storage and secrets
CSP: content security policy, a header listing which content sources a page may use
CSV: comma-separated values, a plain-text table format
CT: computed tomography, a medical scan built from many X-ray images
DDA: digital differential analyser, a line-drawing algorithm that adds fractional increments
DI: dependency injection, handing a class its dependencies instead of letting it create them
DIP: dependency inversion principle, the D in SOLID
DJL: Deep Java Library, Amazon's library for running models from Java
DKIM: DomainKeys Identified Mail, a signature proving an email came from the domain
DMARC: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance
DRY: don't repeat yourself, keep each piece of knowledge in one place
DTO: data transfer object, a plain shape for data crossing a boundary such as a request body
DWARF: the debugging data format that accompanies ELF binaries
E2E: end to end, a test that drives the whole running application the way a user does
ECDH: elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman, a key exchange on an elliptic curve
ELK: Elasticsearch, Logstash and Kibana, a log search stack
EMV: expected monetary value, the probability-weighted average payoff of a decision
EOQ: economic order quantity, the order size that balances ordering and holding costs
ESO: External Secrets Operator, syncing secrets from a manager into Kubernetes
EV: expected value, the probability-weighted average of the outcomes
EVPI: expected value of perfect information, the most any information about an uncertain outcome can be worth
EXIF: exchangeable image file format, the metadata cameras and phones store inside photos, such as the time, orientation and GPS location
FAISS: Facebook AI Similarity Search, a library for fast nearest-neighbour search over vectors
FIN: finish, the TCP flag that begins a connection teardown
FPM: FastCGI Process Manager, PHP's pool of worker processes (PHP-FPM)
GBNF: GGML Backus–Naur form, llama.cpp's grammar format for restricting which tokens a model may generate
GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation, the EU and UK law on personal data
GGML: the tensor library underneath llama.cpp; the letters are its author Georgi Gerganov's initials plus ML (machine learning)
GGUF: the model file format used by llama.cpp and Ollama, holding quantised weights
GHASH: the Galois hash used by GCM
GIF: Graphics Interchange Format, an image format
GNU: GNU's Not Unix, the free-software project behind GCC and the core Unix tools
GORM: the best-known ORM library for Go
GPS: Global Positioning System, the satellite system phones use to know where they are
GPTQ: a post-training quantisation method for GPU inference
H2: an in-memory Java database often used in tests
HMAC: hash-based message authentication code, a keyed hash that proves a message wasn't changed
HNSW: hierarchical navigable small world, an index for fast approximate nearest-neighbour search
HOT: heap-only tuple (a PostgreSQL update that adds no index entries)
HSTS: HTTP strict transport security, a header requiring HTTPS
HyDE: hypothetical document embeddings: search with a drafted answer instead of the question
IDOR: insecure direct object reference, reading someone else's record by changing an ID
IEEE: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, the body behind standards such as IEEE 754 floating point
INI: initialisation file, a simple key=value configuration format
ISO: International Organization for Standardization, the body behind standards such as ISO 8601 dates
ISR: incremental static regeneration, rebuilding static pages after deploy
IV: initialisation vector, a random value that makes encryption of the same message differ
JPEG: Joint Photographic Experts Group, the common photo format
JPMS: Java Platform Module System, the module-info.java modules added in Java 9
JSONB: binary JSON, Postgres's indexed JSON column type
JSONL: JSON Lines, a text format with one complete JSON object per line
JSSE: Java Secure Socket Extension, Java's built-in TLS implementation
JWKS: JSON Web Key Set, the published list of public keys used to check a JWT's signature
KISS: keep it simple, stupid, prefer the simplest solution that meets the requirement
KKT: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions, the optimality conditions for inequality-constrained optimisation
LINQ: Language Integrated Query, C#'s built-in query methods such as Where, Select and Count
LP: linear program, an optimisation model with a linear objective and linear constraints; in DeFi, a liquidity provider
LQR: linear–quadratic regulator, an optimal controller for linear systems with a quadratic cost
LSP: Liskov substitution principle, the L in SOLID
LTS: long-term support, a release kept patched for years rather than months
MCP: Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting models to tools and data sources
MDC: mapped diagnostic context, per-thread values added to every Java log line
MDN: MDN Web Docs (originally Mozilla Developer Network), the standard free reference for HTML, CSS and JavaScript
MILP: mixed-integer linear program, a linear program in which some variables must be whole numbers
MIP: mixed-integer program, usually the same as a mixed-integer linear program
MPC: model predictive control, which re-solves an optimisation problem at every control step
MRR: mean reciprocal rank: 1 for a right result ranked first, 1/2 for second, and so on, averaged
MSAA: multisample antialiasing, extra coverage samples per pixel but one shading sample
NATS: a lightweight open-source messaging system for publish/subscribe and streams
NDC: normalised device coordinates, the [-1, 1] cube after the perspective divide
NIST: National Institute of Standards and Technology, the US standards body
NULL: the SQL value meaning no value at all, not zero or empty text
NURBS: non-uniform rational B-splines, the standard curve and surface representation in CAD
OCI: Open Container Initiative, the standard format for container images and how they run
OCP: open/closed principle, the O in SOLID
OCR: optical character recognition, reading text from an image
ONNX: Open Neural Network Exchange, a file format for trained models that many runtimes can load
OPT: the EDNS0 option pseudo-record in DNS
OTLP: OpenTelemetry Protocol, the standard way programs send traces, metrics and logs to a collector
OWASP: Open Worldwide Application Security Project, which publishes lists of the most common security risks
p50: 50th percentile, the median: half of values are at or below it
p90: 90th percentile: 9 in 10 values are at or below it
p95: 95th percentile: 19 in 20 values are at or below it
p99: 99th percentile: 99 in 100 values are at or below it
p999: 99.9th percentile: 999 in 1,000 values are at or below it
PEM: privacy-enhanced mail, the text format for keys and certificates that starts with -----BEGIN
PERT: program evaluation and review technique, project scheduling with uncertain activity durations
PHC: Password Hashing Competition, whose string format ($argon2id$v=19$...) is the standard way to store a password hash with its settings
PHP: PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, a server-side scripting language
PII: personally identifiable information, data that identifies a person directly or in combination
PKCE: proof key for code exchange, protecting OAuth logins in apps that can't keep a secret
PKCS: Public-Key Cryptography Standards, a family of formats such as PKCS#12
PKI: public key infrastructure, the system of certificates and authorities
PNG: Portable Network Graphics, a lossless image format
POODLE: Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption (an attack)
POSIX: Portable Operating System Interface, the standard Unix programming interface
PPM: portable pixmap, a plain-text image format
PRNG: pseudo-random number generator, an algorithm whose 'random' numbers are fixed by its seed
QP: quadratic program, an optimisation model with a quadratic objective and linear constraints
QUIC: QUIC, a transport protocol over UDP (originally "Quick UDP Internet Connections")
RAND: the RAND Corporation, a US research institute (from 'research and development')
RBAC: role-based access control: deciding what someone may do by their role
RE2: Google's regular-expression library and design, which matches in time proportional to the input and has no lookarounds
RED: rate, errors, duration, the request-centric monitoring signals
ReDoS: regular-expression denial of service: input crafted to make a backtracking pattern take exponential time
RFC: request for comments, the document series that specifies internet protocols
RLHF: reinforcement learning from human feedback, training a model toward the answers people preferred
RLS: row-level security, database rules limiting which rows a user can see
ROUGE: recall-oriented understudy for gisting evaluation, a family of overlap scores for summaries
RPM: requests per minute, a rate limit on how many calls you may make
RRF: reciprocal rank fusion, which combines several rankings by position rather than by score
RST: reset, the TCP flag that aborts a connection
SAML: Security Assertion Markup Language, an older single sign-on standard
SDL: schema definition language, the language GraphQL schemas are written in
SHA: secure hash algorithm; in Git, the hash identifying a commit
SLA: service level agreement, a contractual reliability promise
SLI: service level indicator, the measured reliability signal
SLO: service level objective, the internal target for an SLI
SMS: short message service, a text message
SOLID: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion
SOP: same-origin policy, the browser rule isolating websites from each other
SOPS: Secrets OPerationS, a tool for encrypting secrets inside config files
SPDY: Google's experimental protocol that became HTTP/2
SPF: Sender Policy Framework, a DNS record listing who may send a domain's email
SPFA: shortest path faster algorithm, a queue-based refinement of Bellman-Ford
SQP: sequential quadratic programming, a method for constrained nonlinear optimisation
SQS: Simple Queue Service, Amazon's managed message queue
SRP: single responsibility principle, the S in SOLID
SSE: server-sent events, a way for a server to stream messages to a client over one HTTP response
SSG: course-code prefix; SSG 511 is the computer graphics course the classical part of the graphics notes follows
SSRF: server-side request forgery, making a server fetch an attacker-chosen URL
SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, an XML-based image format that can contain scripts
SWE: software engineering, or a software engineer
SYN: synchronise, the TCP flag that opens a connection
TAP: a virtual network interface carrying Ethernet frames
TBRL: top, bottom, right, left: the bit order of a Cohen-Sutherland region code
TDD: test-driven development, writing a failing test before the code
TGI: Text Generation Inference, Hugging Face's model server
TPM: tokens per minute, a rate limit on how many tokens you may send and receive
TTFT: time to first token, how long until the first piece of a streamed reply arrives
TUN: a virtual network interface carrying IP packets
USSD: unstructured supplementary service data, menus reached by dialling a short code on a phone
UUID: universally unique identifier, a 128-bit ID such as 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
VCR: videocassette recorder; also a Ruby library that records HTTP calls and replays them in tests
VPS: virtual private server, a rented virtual machine you run your own software on
VRP: vehicle routing problem, the multi-vehicle version of the travelling salesman problem
W3C: World Wide Web Consortium, the body that publishes web standards such as HTML and the traceparent header
WSGI: web server gateway interface, Python's standard interface between web servers and apps
YAGNI: you aren't gonna need it, don't build for a requirement that hasn't arrived
YAML: YAML Ain't Markup Language, a configuration file format
§: section: “§4” means section 4 of the note
EOF: end of file: the point where there's nothing more to read
FFI: foreign function interface, calling code written in another language
RAII: resource acquisition is initialisation: a value cleans up after itself when it goes out of scope, like a lock unlocking
RDS: Relational Database Service, Amazon's managed databases
TOML: Tom's Obvious, Minimal Language, the settings format Cargo.toml uses
WASM: WebAssembly, a compact program format that runs in browsers and other hosts
MAC: message authentication code, a short code made from a message and a secret key that proves the message wasn't changed
AUC: area under the curve, here the area under the ROC curve
CART: Classification and Regression Trees, a decision tree algorithm that splits using Gini impurity
CPT: conditional probability table, the probabilities of a node in a Bayesian network given its parents
CUDA: Compute Unified Device Architecture, NVIDIA's platform for running code on its GPUs
DBSCAN: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise
FN: false negative: predicted No, but the real answer is Yes
FOIL: First-Order Inductive Learner, an early inductive logic programming system
FP: false positive: predicted Yes, but the real answer is No
ID3: Iterative Dichotomiser 3, a decision tree algorithm that splits using entropy and information gain
IG: information gain, the drop in entropy after a split
OPTICS: Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure
ROC: receiver operating characteristic, the curve of true positive rate against false positive rate
SAR: structure–activity relationship, how a molecule's structure affects what it does
SNE: stochastic neighbour embedding, as in t-SNE
TN: true negative: predicted No, and the real answer is No
TP: true positive: predicted Yes, and the real answer is Yes
TPR: true positive rate (recall or sensitivity), TP / (TP + FN)
DER: Distinguished Encoding Rules, a compact binary format for keys and certificates
EC: elliptic curve, the kind of key used by ES256 signatures
SIGTERM: the signal that politely asks a program to stop; docker stop, Kubernetes and systemd send it
SIGINT: the signal Ctrl+C sends to a program running in a terminal
AHP: Analytical Hierarchy Process, a method for choosing between options by comparing criteria two at a time
ASME: American Society of Mechanical Engineers, a body that publishes design standards
ASTM: American Society for Testing and Materials, a body that publishes material and testing standards
CNC: computer numerical control, machines that cut parts automatically from a computer file
CPSC: Consumer Product Safety Commission, the US agency that sets safety rules for consumer products
DFMA: design for manufacturing and assembly, designing a product so it is easy and cheap to make and put together
DHS: Department of Homeland Security, a US government department
DSM: design structure matrix, a table showing which parts of a design interact with each other
EPA: Environmental Protection Agency, the US agency that protects health and the environment
FMEA: failure mode and effects analysis, listing how each part could fail, what happens, and what to do about it
HFE: human factors engineering, designing so people can operate a product efficiently and safely
OSHA: Occupational Safety and Health Administration, the US agency for workplace safety
PET: polyethylene terephthalate, the thermoplastic used for drink bottles
PVC: polyvinyl chloride, a thermoplastic used for pipes
QFD: quality function deployment, turning customer needs into specific design requirements
ROI: return on investment, how much is gained compared with what was spent
RPN: risk priority number, severity × occurrence × detection in an FMEA
SCAMPER: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Rearrange: seven questions for new ideas
SON: Standards Organisation of Nigeria, the body that sets product standards in Nigeria
TIG: tungsten inert gas, a precise kind of welding
TLC: total life cycle, a product's whole life from raw material to recycling or disposal
TRIZ: Theory of Inventive Problem Solving (from the Russian name), with its 40 inventive principles
